key_insight: TEPID-ADAPT-VQE can simultaneously target and accurately recover multiple low-lying molecular excited states by variationally diagonalizing a truncated thermal density matrix.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a near-term quantum chemistry workflow with compact adaptive circuits and only one main tuning knob, making excited-state simulation more practical to deploy.
method: Build a truncated low-temperature Gibbs state to represent the targeted excited-state manifold.
Use ADAPT to grow a compact, problem-tailored ansatz during optimization.
Compare against a modified MORE-ADAPT-VQE baseline across multiple molecules and bond lengths.
evidence_signal: Across H2, LiH, and linear H4 over weakly and strongly correlated geometries, both TEPID-ADAPT and MORE-ADAPT reproduced excited-state spectra and potential energy curves within chemical accuracy.
watch_item: Performance depends on choosing an appropriate temperature hyperparameter, which must still be matched to the target energy scale and system.
paper_title: Quantum simulation of molecular excited-state manifolds and energies using the TEPID-ADAPT-VQE algorithm
